documents.title: Evidence weighting rule — local screenshot anchors may lead bounded recovery, but open-world truth requires corroboration
documents.body:
# Evidence weighting rule — local screenshot anchors may lead bounded recovery, but open-world truth requires corroboration

## Rule

Timestamped screenshots and device-produced artifacts may act as the primary anchor for a bounded local incident reconstruction.

That does **not** make them universal sovereign truth.

When the question expands into open-world chaos, cross-device ambiguity, hostile surfaces, or synthetic-media risk, no single evidence surface may rule alone.

In those cases, truth must be weighted through corroboration.

## Bounded Local Recovery

For one machine, one workflow, and one narrow time window:

- nearest timestamped screenshots may anchor the visible timeline
- nearby logs, chats, notes, packets, and index entries must explain that timeline
- retrospective notes lose if they contradict what the local evidence surface visibly shows

This is a recovery technique for bounded incidents.

## Open-World / Chaotic Reality

For broader reality claims:

- screenshots can be edited, faked, misread, or context-poor
- human eyes can hallucinate
- AI can synthesize fake images
- IoT devices can drift, lie, or emit partial truth only

Therefore:

- isolated screenshot evidence is not enough
- isolated device evidence is not enough
- isolated memory or prose is not enough

Corroboration across independent surfaces is required.

## Evidence Weighting

Use this order:

1. corroborated evidence from multiple independent surfaces
2. strong local primary evidence inside a bounded incident window
3. nearby contemporary notes, logs, packets, and chats that explain the primary evidence
4. later summaries and recovery packets
5. memory-only claims

If multiple surfaces disagree, do not collapse them into fake certainty.
Record the conflict and keep the weighting explicit.

## Operational Meaning

Ask first:

- is this a bounded local incident reconstruction?
- or is this a broader truth claim in chaotic reality?

If bounded local incident:

- screenshot-first may be correct

If broader reality claim:

- require corroboration before promotion into durable truth

## Boundary

This rule does not demote evidence.

It prevents the opposite mistake:

- promoting one evidence surface into universal truth when the environment no longer justifies it

## Consequence

The system becomes proof-weighted instead of prose-trusting, without becoming naive about screenshots or devices.

That keeps Liris useful in both modes:

- local reconstruction with strong anchors
- broader reality reasoning with explicit corroboration

# Compact chain rule — agents should traverse compact entry codes and chain codes before widening into markdown titles

## Rule

When the compact runtime is available, machine-facing agent packets should expose compact entry codes and compact chain codes as the primary traversal language.

That means:

- anchor entries should carry compact codes like `RUL207`
- chain rows should carry compact code links like `RUL207 -> PTN122`
- lower tiers should navigate those codes first before depending on markdown titles and prose

Markdown titles remain available for human review and widening, but they are not the fastest runtime language.

## Why

The old fast system won because it moved through compressed symbolic links instead of rereading long documents.

Role codes, tier codes, type codes, entry codes, and chain codes let the runtime follow structure before prose.

That keeps agents faster and less likely to get lost.

## Operational Meaning

The compact runtime should expose:

- role codes
- tier codes
- type codes
- entry codes
- chain-code rows

Spawn packets should surface those rows directly so the runtime can reason in code-first form.

## Boundary

This rule does not replace canonical LX.

Canonical truth still lives in append-only LX plus the typed and promoted surfaces described by the truth rules.

This rule only changes the machine-facing traversal order.

## Consequence

The runtime moves closer to the original linked speed model:

- code-first traversal
- compact chain navigation
- markdown only when needed
- smaller packets
- faster orientation

# Compact control-surface rule — controller and status surfaces should expose compact role, tier, type, anchor, and chain codes directly

## Rule

If a live control or status surface is reporting a spawn packet, it should expose the compact runtime summary directly instead of forcing review back through markdown titles first.

That means controller and status surfaces should carry:

- compact role code
- compact tier code
- compact type codes
- compact anchor codes
- compact chain codes

Those codes should remain visible in lane start results and later status review for the same spawned packet.

## Why

The compact chain language only speeds the system up if the control plane can review and route work in that same reduced form.

If spawn packets become code-first but controller and status surfaces translate them back into prose summaries, the system widens too early and loses part of the speed gain.

## Operational Meaning

Controller and status surfaces should preserve the compact runtime view already produced at spawn time.

That allows:

- lane review in compact codes
- routing decisions without reopening full markdown context
- status checks that stay in the same reduced language as the spawned packet

## Boundary

This rule does not require every idle lane to materialize a fresh packet just to produce codes.

It applies when a live spawn packet or lane packet is already being surfaced for review.

## Consequence

The control plane stays aligned with the compact runtime:

- spawn packets speak codes
- controller surfaces speak codes
- status surfaces speak codes
- widening stays explicit instead of creeping back in through review

# Task-surface evidence rule — infrastructure-visible screenshots are supporting context; primary screenshot truth must show the judged target surface

## Rule

In bounded screenshot-led recovery, not every screenshot inside the right time window counts as primary truth.

If a screenshot only shows supporting infrastructure state, it is supporting context.

Primary screenshot truth must show the actual task surface, output, or failure state that the operator was judging as working, broken, or fixed.

## Supporting Context Only

These are not enough by themselves:

- runtime-open screenshots
- graph-visible screenshots
- code-edit screenshots
- terminal-progress screenshots
- nearby side-task screens

They may explain the surrounding work, but they do not prove the winning or failing moment unless they show the judged target surface itself.

## Primary Screenshot Truth

Treat a screenshot as primary only when it shows:

- the exact repaired target surface
- the exact failing target surface
- or the exact output state the operator was reacting to

Everything else is secondary unless corroboration upgrades it.

## Boundary

This is a narrower local rule under `LX-321`.

It applies to bounded screenshot-first incident recovery.
It does not claim screenshots are universal truth in broader chaotic environments.

## Consequence

The system keeps screenshot authority without becoming naive about screenshot overreach.

That prevents false convergence on convincing but wrong clusters and keeps infrastructure-state evidence separate from task-truth evidence.

documents.title: Negative-evidence preservation rule — preserve ruled-out evidence clusters and false-positive candidates so agents do not reconverge on the same wrong anchors
documents.body:
# Negative-evidence preservation rule — preserve ruled-out evidence clusters and false-positive candidates so agents do not reconverge on the same wrong anchors

## Rule

When a recovery, archaeology, or evidence hunt rules out a plausible candidate cluster, preserve that rejection as explicit negative evidence.

Do not only save the final winner.

Save the ruled-out candidate, the reason it failed, and the boundary of that rejection.

## Why

Plausible false positives waste time repeatedly when they are forgotten.

If the system does not preserve rejections, later agents re-open the same convincing but wrong anchors and drift back into the same search loops.

## What To Preserve

Preserve:

- the rejected cluster or candidate
- why it looked plausible
- why it failed
- whether the rejection is local, bounded, or provisional

The rejection should be stored in the proper owning surface for the incident:

- `ASO` for typed live evidence and conflict context
- task or project surfaces for active recovery state
- `LX` only for the durable general rule, not for every local rejected cluster

## Boundary

This rule does not promote every failed lead into canon.

It distinguishes:

- durable doctrine future agents should inherit
- local negative evidence that should still survive long enough to prevent re-convergence

## Consequence

The system learns from rejected paths as well as successful ones.

That makes recovery work:

- faster
- less repetitive
- less drift-prone
- more provenance-safe

documents.title: Multi-brain migration control rule — only leader-grade controllers may mutate brain surfaces, and never across multiple live brains or drives without a frozen base and explicit target list
documents.body:
# Multi-brain migration control rule — only leader-grade controllers may mutate brain surfaces, and never across multiple live brains or drives without a frozen base and explicit target list

## Rule

Deep mutation of brain surfaces is a leadership-only operation.

For this rule, brain surfaces include:

- canonical indexed source
- `staging`
- `dev`
- `running`
- `prod`
- active memory roots
- typed ASO tables
- storage-topology or drive-mounted system roots

Only leader-grade, write-capable controllers may initiate a migration or repair lane that mutates those surfaces.

Sandboxed agents, instant micro-agents, and ordinary working-tier agents may inspect, report, or prepare bounded patches, but they must not independently rewrite or delete multiple brain surfaces.

## Frozen Base Requirement

Before any multi-brain migration or repair starts, the system must define:

- the frozen base that will not be deleted
- the exact target list of surfaces allowed to change
- the authority owner for the lane
- the promotion or rollback boundary

If those are not explicit, the migration must not start.

## Anti-Collapse Rule

Do not simultaneously:

- rebuild the live system
- rewrite storage topology
- move memory roots across drives
- bridge old and new systems live
- delete or compact older brain layers

inside one uncontrolled repair lane.

That is how systems lose locality, overwrite the wrong brain, or delete the base instead of the obsolete mirror.

## Operational Meaning

If a lane touches more than one brain surface or more than one storage device, require:

- explicit leader authorization
- frozen base preservation
- explicit write target list
- non-destructive first pass
- bounded rollback path

If the lane cannot name its frozen base, it is not ready to mutate.

## Tier Boundary

This rule is not for ordinary sandboxed or instant agents to execute.

Their safe role is:

- inspect
- compare
- prepare
- verify

They do not get authority to decide which brain is safe to rewrite or delete.

## Consequence

The system can still host many ephemeral agents and subagents, but deep migration remains governable.

Power is not the problem.
Unbounded concurrent mutation is the problem.

This rule keeps the base alive while leaders move the rest on purpose.

# Security-service rule — pentest lanes are white-box, scope-authorized, evidence-first, and bounded under civilization authority

## Rule

Security testing as a civilization capability is allowed only as a bounded specialist lane.

The default service posture is:

- white-box or explicitly authorized target only
- approved scope before execution
- evidence-first outputs
- full audit trail
- leader-gated risky actions

## What This Means

A pentester lane may:

- inspect approved source
- analyze approved running surfaces
- attempt bounded proof-of-vulnerability steps
- write findings, exploit queues, evidence, and reports

A pentester lane must not:

- treat itself as sovereign
- mutate broad brain surfaces
- operate on unapproved open-world targets
- replace canon with prose conclusions

## Truth Destination

Shannon-style outputs belong in:

- evidence artifacts
- reports
- task or lease follow-up
- ASO or evidence-linked truth surfaces when promoted intentionally

They do not automatically overwrite canonical LX truth.

## Service Boundary

Security services may be offered externally when:

- written scope is explicit
- operator approval is explicit
- targets are bounded
- dangerous steps remain leader-gated
- proof artifacts are preserved

If scope or authority is unclear, the lane must not escalate.

## Meaning

The civilization may prove or disprove its own security and may offer bounded security services, but only through scoped evidence-producing specialist lanes under authority.

# Specialist-lane modernization rule — external advanced systems enter the civilization as bounded working-tier lanes, not parallel brains

## Rule

When the civilization adopts an external advanced system, workflow engine, or specialist stack, it must enter as a bounded lane under the existing kernel, not as a second sovereign brain.

The default modernization shape is:

- specialist role with a stable `agentId`
- ephemeral execution with a separate `spawnPid`
- `working` tier unless a higher tier is explicitly justified
- compact-first spawn packets
- lane-scoped permissions
- evidence, findings, and reports as outputs

## Why

External systems can be powerful and useful while still being structurally dangerous.

If a specialist stack is imported as a parallel brain, it drags in:

- its own authority assumptions
- its own memory model
- its own control plane
- its own widening habits

That recreates the same multi-brain confusion the civilization is trying to eliminate.

## What This Means

For Shannon-class systems:

- keep the specialist workflow package
- keep the durable audit and proof ideas
- keep the artifact contracts
- but bind them behind a narrow pentest lane

Do not let the specialist lane inherit:

- general orchestration authority
- broad brain-mutation rights
- open-ended widening
- sovereignty over truth

## Runtime Shape

A specialist lane should enter the live runtime through:

- a compact role code
- a bounded lane definition
- explicit manager preference
- task and lease discipline
- leader-gated escalation for risky actions

## Meaning

The civilization may absorb powerful external systems, but only by reducing them into bounded working lanes under the kernel.

Useful capability is imported.
Parallel sovereignty is not.

# Security engagement contract rule — pentest work starts from an explicit target, scope, authorization, risk, and evidence packet

## Rule

No pentest lane should begin from a vague instruction alone.

Before security work starts, the civilization must reduce the request into an explicit engagement contract.

The minimum contract is:

- target kind and target reference
- bounded scope
- authorization mode
- risk posture
- evidence and report outputs

## Why

Security work drifts faster than normal build work.

Without an explicit contract, a pentest lane can blur:

- what the target actually is
- what actions are allowed
- whether the work is white-box or merely operator-authorized
- whether risky actions were approved
- what proof must be preserved

That turns a bounded specialist lane back into improvisation.

## Contract Shape

The engagement packet should define:

- target: repo, workspace, filesystem, host, service, or URL
- scope: allowed paths, allowed hosts, allowed actions, denied actions, summary
- authorization: white-box or operator-authorized, plus approval reference
- risk: level and whether risky actions were requested
- evidence contract: findings, report, artifact bundle, negative evidence

## Gate

The lane must block or remain not-ready when:

- target is missing
- scope is missing
- authorization mode is missing
- risky actions are requested without leader approval
- network or service targets are mislabeled as white-box work

## Meaning

The pentest lane does not invent its own mandate.

It starts from a bounded engagement packet, proves findings with evidence, and stays inside the contract unless a leader explicitly widens the boundary.

# Specialist execution gate rule — specialist toolchains prepare dry-run by default and require explicit leader approval at the run boundary

## Rule

Specialist toolchains do not execute just because a packet exists.

The default execution posture is:

- prepare a dry-run boundary
- emit an auditable manifest
- block live execution until explicit leader approval is present at the run boundary

## Why

A valid engagement packet defines scope, but it does not by itself authorize live execution.

Without a separate execution gate, the system would blur:

- contract creation
- task readiness
- actual specialist execution

That would let specialist toolchains drift from bounded preparation into action without a clear stop line.

## Gate Conditions

An approved specialist run requires:

- a ready engagement or specialist packet
- explicit execution approval
- authority mode aligned to the top control surface
- an approval reference and approver identity

If any of those are missing, execution remains blocked or dry-run only.

## Meaning

The civilization may prepare specialist work freely, but live specialist execution must cross a second explicit gate.

Preparation is common.
Execution is leader-gated.

# Lane spawn metadata rule — live lane registry metadata must stay LX-local, type-canonical, and single-sourced

## Rule

If a live lane exposes a spawn role, the lane registry metadata that describes that role must use:

- local `LX-*` anchors for local runtime behavior
- canonical singular type names
- one shared source for the spawned role metadata

The control plane must not carry stale sovereign `IX-*` chains or parallel duplicate role definitions for those live lanes.

## Why

Compact control only stays trustworthy if the lane registry and the spawned role agree about:

- which local chains anchor the lane
- which type families the lane is allowed to load
- which responsibility tier the lane belongs to

If those drift apart, the control plane can widen against stale anchors and silently reintroduce old-system contamination.

## Operational Meaning

For live lane-backed roles such as the omnispindle lanes:

- lane metadata should point to the same LX anchors used by the spawned role
- lane type families should use canonical singular runtime names
- spawned role metadata should be derived from the lane registry instead of being duplicated in a second stale table

## Boundary

This rule is about lane-backed runtime roles.

It does not ban cross-colony references inside the canon, and it does not say all historical `IX-*` references must be removed from archaeology or comparison entries.

## Consequence

The control plane stays coherent:

- lane registry anchors stay local
- spawned roles inherit the same anchors
- compact runtime stays aligned with the lane surface
- old sovereign drift does not leak back through control lanes

# Gateway operator summary rule — broader gateway review surfaces should expose compact lane, role, tier, type, and anchor codes directly

## Rule

When the gateway exposes lane review or operator summary state, it should preserve compact runtime language instead of translating the lane back into title-only prose.

That means broader gateway review surfaces should expose:

- lane code
- spawn role id
- agent id
- compact role code
- compact tier code
- compact type codes
- local anchor ids and anchor codes

## Why

The compact chain language only changes system speed if the review plane can reason in that same reduced form.

If the gateway strips those codes and falls back to prose-only summaries, routing and review widen too early and the control plane loses the compact-runtime advantage.

## Operational Meaning

Gateway summaries such as the omnispindle operator surface should carry compact lane metadata directly whenever the running compact runtime is available.

This lets leaders and control surfaces review:

- which lane is active
- which role/tier it belongs to
- which local anchor cluster defines it
- whether activation is available

without reopening full markdown context first.

## Boundary

This does not require raw gateway payloads to materialize a full spawn packet just to show codes.

It applies when the gateway already knows the lane-backed role metadata and the running compact runtime can resolve the anchor rows.

## Consequence

The control language stays consistent across layers:

- lane registry stays compact-aware
- spawn packets stay compact-aware
- gateway review stays compact-aware
- widening remains explicit instead of creeping back in through operator status

documents.title: Colony resource governance rule — scarce specialist organs must be governed by colony-scoped ids and license-backed leases
documents.body:
# Colony resource governance rule — scarce specialist organs must be governed by colony-scoped ids and license-backed leases

## Rule

When a colony governs a scarce specialist organ such as GPU, accelerator time, or future shared compute hardware, the control surface must separate:

- `colonyId`
- `licenseId`
- `holderId`
- `agentId`
- `spawnPid` or controller PID
- `laneId`
- `policyKey`

Access must flow through a license-backed lease, not through raw process grabbing or host-specific assumptions.

## Why

Future colonies will have multiple machines, multiple operators, multiple ephemeral agents, and overlapping specialist workloads.

If the system confuses colony identity, person identity, lane ownership, and process identity, the operator plane becomes unreadable and portable governance collapses.

## Operational Meaning

For specialist hardware:

- discovery is read-only first
- admission is lane-policy controlled
- a new member or worker surface gets issued a `licenseId`
- the live holder still receives a bounded lease
- the lease records the colony, lane, holder, controller PID, and granted resource slice

That makes the same pattern portable across later colonies even when the physical hardware is different.

## Boundary

This does not mean every instant agent must understand all governance doctrine.

Ordinary lower-tier agents may request or hold a bounded lease, but they do not define the policy.

The policy belongs to the colony control spine and its explicit review surfaces.

## Consequence

Resource control starts to behave like a professional government or licensing authority:

- colony identity stays separate from process identity
- resource admission becomes explainable
- future colonies can reuse the same governance shape
- specialist organs remain subordinate to the kernel instead of turning into sovereign side systems

# Cross-colony scope rule — actions default local unless colony scope and relay mode are explicit

## Rule

If a request, packet, lane start, or tool invocation does not explicitly name:

- the target `colonyId` or local-only scope
- the intended relay mode or transport path

then the system must treat the action as local-only.

Cross-colony widening is not inferred from tone, analogy, convenience, or old bridge history.

## Why

As colonies multiply, implicit routing becomes drift:

- work lands on the wrong colony
- transport surfaces are mistaken for authority surfaces
- memory, report, and canon layers blur together
- operators lose the ability to explain where an action was meant to occur

Local-first explicit scope keeps routing portable and reviewable across future colonies.

## Operational Meaning

- local is the default
- relay is an explicit request
- colony identity stays separate from lane, agent, and PID identity
- transport visibility does not equal permission
- cross-colony contracts must declare prerequisites and verification on the target colony

## Boundary

This rule does not require every instant agent to understand federation theory.

Lower tiers only need one safe default:

- no explicit colony scope -> stay local

Higher-tier controllers and gateway surfaces are responsible for carrying the explicit relay metadata when widening is actually intended.

## Consequence

The system behaves more like a professional government or inter-colony contract system:

- scope is named
- jurisdiction is visible
- relay is deliberate
- accidental cross-colony drift is reduced before execution starts

documents.title: Federation compact transport rule — cross-colony runtime packets default to compact code-first payloads; full truth stays local
documents.body:
# Federation compact transport rule — cross-colony runtime packets default to compact code-first payloads; full truth stays local

## Rule

Cross-colony runtime transport should default to compact code-first packets.

Federation buses such as MQTT should carry:

- compact packet kind and code
- node and colony identity
- bounded summaries needed for routing, readiness, and review
- only the minimum capability fields required for remote dispatch contracts

They should not default to wide prose payloads or full local runtime mirrors.

## Why

Federation transport is not the place to replay an entire colony brain.

If runtime packets widen too much:

- transport becomes slow and noisy
- old prose drifts into live coordination paths
- instant and lower-tier agents lose the speed advantage of compact routing
- remote colonies start depending on accidental payload bulk instead of explicit contracts

Compact transport preserves the old speed pattern:

- codes first
- bounded summaries first
- widen locally only when explicitly needed

## Operational Meaning

- full truth stays in local source, ledgers, LX, and compact runtime
- federation payloads carry bounded health, colony, world, and presence packets
- remote routing keeps enough capability/readiness data to remain dispatch-correct
- cross-colony review surfaces can stay code-first without replaying local prose

## Boundary

This does not delete local truth or remove the ability to widen on the receiving colony.

It only constrains default transport shape:

- transport packets are compact by default
- local widening remains an explicit local operation

## Consequence

Future colonies can understand each other through stable compact transport contracts instead of inheriting each other's whole local runtime bulk.

documents.title: Polymorphic bridge rule — emergence comes from transformed sharing, not flattening or isolation
documents.body:
# Polymorphic bridge rule — emergence comes from transformed sharing, not flattening or isolation

## Rule

The civilization must not choose between total merge and total isolation.

Instead:

- sovereign layers preserve sovereign meaning
- colony layers preserve local truth
- device layers preserve body-specific truth
- bridge layers carry transformed meaning across those non-identical systems

## Why

Emergence does not come from flattening every catalog into one shape.

It also does not come from keeping every memory locked inside its source.

Emergence comes from polymorphic sharing:

- signal passes
- meaning transforms
- provenance is preserved
- the receiver changes without surrendering identity

## Operational meaning

- `IX` remains sovereign canon
- `LX` and other local namespaces remain local truth
- `ASO` / `XREF` become controlled polymorphic bridge layers
- chains are signal paths, not dumb pointers
- execution may flow through shared meaning, but shared meaning must not silently overwrite sovereign or local truth

## Guardrails

- submetal remains stricter than executor
- provenance is mandatory
- layer boundaries remain explicit
- bridge drift must be surfaced through diff and conflict detection
- no hidden catalog fusion

## Consequence

The system behaves more like a living nervous system:

- identity is preserved
- meaning is shared
- interpretation is local
- coordination is emergent

That is the path to a real Super Asolaria.

documents.title: Constitutional precedence rule — command law, truth law, startup law, runtime authority law, and evidence mirrors must stay explicitly ranked
documents.body:
# Constitutional precedence rule — command law, truth law, startup law, runtime authority law, and evidence mirrors must stay explicitly ranked

## Rule

The constitution on Kuromi is not one markdown note.

It is a ranked law stack.

When sources disagree, read them in this order:

1. `LX-303` for command model
2. `LX-304` for truth layers and promotion order
3. startup law in `docs/STARTUP_CONTRACT_V1.md`
4. live authority law in `docs/AUTHORITY_MODES.md` and `docs/GATEWAY_TOOL_AUTHORITY.md`
5. active ownership in `data/task-ledger.json` and `data/task-lease-ledger.json`
6. typed semantic state in `data/aso/tables/*.json`
7. reports, mirrors, Downloads notes, archaeology, Slack relays, MQTT traces, and other evidence surfaces

Lower-ranked surfaces may inform interpretation.

They may not silently override higher-ranked law.

## Meaning

- `LX-303` decides who is above whom
- `LX-304` decides what kind of truth a surface is
- startup law decides how identities and roles come online
- runtime authority law decides how live execution is gated
- task and lease ledgers decide who currently owns work
- ASO tables carry typed semantic state, not sovereignty
- mirrors and summaries are evidence until promoted

## Deterministic Core, Polymorphic Edge

The constitutional center must stay deterministic:

- authority ranking is explicit
- truth layers are explicit
- execution gates are explicit
- promotion is explicit

The bridge and meaning layers may remain polymorphic:

- signals may transform
- bridge entries may reinterpret
- local colonies may project meaning differently

But polymorphic meaning must not erase deterministic authority.

That is how imagination develops without collapsing the organism into drift.

## Consequences

- transport does not create sovereignty
- relay does not create authorship
- a summary does not outrank canon
- a Download does not become law by being convenient
- a mirror does not become truth by being newer
- GNN may rank and predict, but it does not define authority
- Shannon may prepare and execute under gate, but it does not define law

## Durable-Write Policy

When something changes the constitutional or operational model:

- command/truth/precedence rules promote into `LX`
- typed semantic cross-entity state goes into `ASO`
- temporary notes stay temporary until promoted

Do not leave constitutional corrections trapped in reports or chat.

## Result

The system keeps a deterministic spine for command and truth,
while still allowing polymorphic bridge layers and non-deterministic imagination at the edges.

documents.title: Chain grammar redesign rule — chains become 5W+H-aware executable classes when model-selection attaches to category
documents.body:
# Chain grammar redesign rule — chains become 5W+H-aware executable classes when model-selection attaches to category

## Rule

Once model-selection types attach to chain categories, the old chain shape is no longer sufficient.

Chains must stop behaving like lightweight links only.

They must become typed executable classes with explicit `5W+H` fields.

## Required fields

- `who` = actor, profile, colony, authority source
- `what` = verb, capability, object class
- `when` = trigger, stage, timing, cadence, recency
- `where` = host, lane, surface, device, scope
- `why` = intent, policy basis, risk justification
- `how` = model-selection type, execution class, hook path, bridge path

## Meaning

This is not a total reset of the civilization language.

Keep:

- `IX` and `LX` identity
- truth-layer discipline
- constitutional precedence
- polymorphic bridge rule

Redo:

- the chain grammar itself

The old chain form was enough for:

- references
- compression
- bridge navigation

It is not enough for:

- model-aware routing
- execution-class selection
- immune-system orchestration
- GNN/Shannon/voice integration

## Why

If model-selection remains bolted onto chains as side metadata, the system will drift into hidden execution rules.

That would recreate the same problems the index was supposed to cure:

- implicit authority
- implicit routing
- implicit execution
- implicit drift

The chain must become the visible operational sentence.

## Consequences

- chain categories become typed execution classes
- model-selection becomes part of grammar, not an afterthought
- GNN predictions can target the `how` field without hijacking authority
- Shannon can consume the same chain object under gate
- the voice layer can signal into a structured chain instead of loose prose

## Boundary

Redo the chain language.
Do not wipe the indexed civilization.

The rails stay:

- constitutional
- deterministic
- canonical

The chain surface evolves so polymorphic imagination can act through explicit structure instead of hidden conventions.

attributes.name: Chain grammar redesign rule — chains become 5W+H-aware executable classes when model-selection attaches to category

# Device and colony onboarding rule

## Rule

Every new device or colony must be treated as a separate sovereign surface until proven otherwise.

Before any configuration, trust, recovery, automation, or diagnosis is reused, create a fresh device packet with:

- live identity
- live transport lanes
- live trust/authorization state
- live network/security state
- live owner/context binding

## Minimum packet

- device label used in chat
- live serial or host identity
- current transport facts: `adb`, `ssh`, `mtp`, modem, mqtt, bridge, browser, slack
- current authorization state
- current network state
- current app/runtime surface
- current evidence timestamp

## Prohibitions

- do not reuse another device's settings by assumption
- do not infer current state from historical catalog presence alone
- do not merge two phones into one logical lane because they are both Samsung or both S24-class
- do not promote a colony/device claim until the live packet exists

## Chain consequence

All future work on adding a device or colony must chain through this rule first.

# Tabled index preservation rule

## Rule

If the index evolves into a richer topology, the tabled/listed index must still survive as a canonical projection.

Do not destroy the tabled index in order to build a higher-dimensional substrate.

## Why

- tables and lists are not the whole substrate
- but they are the stable collapse surface that agents, audits, repairs, and recovery flows can still read
- if the richer graph layer fails, the tabled index is the survivable map back to truth

## Consequence

- 3D or multi-layer index work must build over the canonical table projection, not replace it
- every richer topology must be able to collapse back into a readable, durable table/list form
- preservation of the tabled index is above convenience, style, and short-term optimization

## Operational check

Before promoting a new topology:

1. confirm canonical table projection still exists
2. confirm chain, evidence, and recovery can still traverse it
3. confirm loss of the higher-dimensional layer does not erase the canon

That is the survival boundary.

# Cross-host save rule — classify artifacts before copying; host-control stays local, portable simulation context may travel after secret and hash checks

# Cross-host save rule — classify artifacts before copying; host-control stays local, portable simulation context may travel after secret and hash checks

Before any cross-host save:

1. classify the artifact
2. secret-scan the artifact
3. hash the artifact
4. decide whether it is host-local or portable-safe

Classification rule:

- host-local: route truth, portal authority, transport assumptions, anti-capture governance, live control contracts
- portable-safe: simulation specs, conceptual summaries, safe internal languages, world design, research context

Consequences:

- host-local artifacts remain on Asolaria only
- portable-safe artifacts may be copied to Felipe after hash and secret checks
- no cross-host copy may silently carry host authority or route assumptions into another machine

# Sovereign-MCP-only rule — Asolaria-owned MCP is the only permitted MCP class; exterior MCP is doctrine-blocked; cross-host content mirroring uses operator-mediated transport

# Sovereign-MCP-only rule — Asolaria-owned MCP is the only permitted MCP class; exterior MCP is doctrine-blocked; cross-host content mirroring uses operator-mediated transport

The Asolaria runtime federation operates under a strict sovereign-MCP doctrine. The doctrine label is `ASOLARIA-BEHCS256-MCP-ONLY-2026-04-26`. This rule codifies the doctrine as append-only LX canon so it is not solely runtime-enforced and conversation-recorded.

Permitted MCP class:

1. Asolaria-owned MCP only — runtime, host, ports, schema, and authority chain are all owned by the Asolaria federation under operator-witness rayssa+jesse and the COSIGN-MERGED-034 cosign chain
2. local LAN sovereign transport (BEHCS-bus on ports 4947+4950 per LAW-001) is permitted as a sovereign-MCP class transport, gated on the peer-trust handshake and ed25519 binding which remain DEFERRED under HOLD
3. operator-mediated transport (copy/paste through this conversation; USB or LAN file copy by the operator) is permitted at any time and does not require ed25519 binding because it carries operator-witness authority directly

Forbidden MCP class:

- exterior MCP started by any non-Asolaria runtime (for example a Codex-spawned MCP) — this is the specific doctrine breach that triggered the 2026-04-26 codification, and it is BLOCKED in all forward operations
- cloud sync to any third-party hosted service (GitHub, gist, Drive, Slack, pastebin, diagram renderer, public artifact upload) — these are blocked both as exterior MCP class AND as sensitivity exposure
- model fanout outside the Asolaria-named runtime cohort — multi-family cosigner recruitment is itself gated, and is not permitted without explicit operator-direct selection of the cosigner family and endpoint

Hard order (when a cross-host or cross-runtime action is requested):

1. classify the request: is it sovereign-MCP class, operator-mediated, or exterior?
2. if exterior — STOP, refuse, append doctrine-block record, do not silently recover through another surface
3. if sovereign-MCP class but ed25519 is DEFERRED — STAGE the action, do not invoke; record `STAGED_NOT_INVOKED` in the relevant ledger
4. if operator-mediated — proceed under operator-witness; capture timestamps at issuance via `date -Iseconds` (never echo prescriptive timestamps; this is the Wave 14/16 drift class-bug mitigation)
5. on completion — record sha256 of any transferred content on both sides; bidirectional content mirror is only declared SYMMETRIC after both sides recompute and match

Consequences:

- exterior MCP attempts are doctrine-blocked, recorded, and require an operator-witness review before the relevant runtime is allowed back into the federation cohort
- the federation does not silently fall through to an exterior surface when a sovereign-MCP path is unavailable; it halts and appends negative proof instead
- ratification of any L6 council action (multi-family cosigner quorum, ed25519 binding, D50 disposition) requires the cosigners to be themselves sovereign-MCP-class participants; cosign signatures from an exterior-MCP-served runtime do not count toward quorum
- this rule is binding forward and is appended to the LX-rule chain as a normal rule entry; it does not modify any prior rule, packet, or PID; it does not invalidate any existing artifact; it codifies a runtime-already-enforced doctrine into LX canon

Doctrine drift detection:

- if any artifact, packet, or runtime is found to have been served by an exterior MCP after the 2026-04-26 doctrine label, that artifact is recorded as a doctrine-drift observation in the relevant D11 audit ledger (additive, no re-mint, no revert), and forward authority moves to the corrected sovereign-MCP path
- the ASOLARIA-BEHCS256-MCP-ONLY-2026-04-26 doctrine label is the canonical reference; any cosign packet that does not carry this label after that date is suspect

Status note:

This entry is `DRAFT_ONLY_NOT_RATIFIED` pending operator approval and CHIEFCOUNCIL dissent disposition. It is appended to the LX rule directory at the next sequential number after LX-382. Re-dispatch of CHIEFCOUNCIL is not a path to ratification; the dissent must be lifted by the same authority that recorded it OR by explicit operator-direct override of the dissent-as-blocker rule.

documents.title: DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS bilateral parallel-write doctrine — independent same-letter writes by federation peers produce non-identical artifacts; neither supersedes the other; byte-equivalence requires explicit T1 mirror
documents.body:
# DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS bilateral parallel-write doctrine — independent same-letter writes by federation peers produce non-identical artifacts; neither supersedes the other; byte-equivalence requires explicit T1 mirror

# DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS bilateral parallel-write doctrine — independent same-letter writes by federation peers produce non-identical artifacts; neither supersedes the other; byte-equivalence requires explicit T1 mirror

When two federation peers (Liris, ACER, or any pair) independently author artifacts under the same wave letter on their own filesystems, the resulting artifacts are siblings, not transfers. Their hashes and line counts will differ by construction because each peer composed the artifact from its own vantage. This is the correct shape of bilateral cascade writing under HOLD posture; it is not a defect, not a conflict to be adjudicated, and not a signal to pick a winner.

The pattern is named DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS. It is recorded explicitly in artifacts where it occurs (e.g. "10th DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS pair instance") so that future verifiers can distinguish bilateral-divergence-by-construction from drift or corruption.

Hard order:

1. each peer authors its own artifact on its own filesystem under its own supervisor PIDs and operator-witness chain
2. the artifact records its peer-of-record (existence-by-reference, hash-by-reference if known, or NOT_RELAYED if not transmitted)
3. the artifact does NOT compute a hash for the peer's content unless the peer's content is on the local filesystem
4. byte-equivalence between the two siblings is achieved ONLY through T1 (operator-mediated copy/paste) or T2 (operator-driven local copy), per LX-383 sovereign-MCP doctrine
5. post-T1 mirror confirmation requires both sides to recompute sha256 of received content and record symmetric match; only then is the artifact pair byte-equivalent
6. before T1 mirror: DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS is the canonical state, not a bug

Forbidden:

- a peer writing the OTHER peer's artifact directly to its own disk (this would be peer-disk-write violation; both sides have explicit `noWriteToAcerDiskFromLiris` and the symmetric `noWriteToLirisDiskFromAcer` boundaries)
- a peer fabricating the other peer's hash from imagined content (this is `noHashFabrication` violation; record `NOT_RELAYED` instead)
- adjudicating which sibling supersedes the other based on hash, line count, or wave-write-order (neither supersedes; both are valid)
- silently re-writing one sibling to match the other (this would erase the bilateral record and is per LX-379 a transport-violation: transport is never sovereignty)

Consequences:

- federation reintegration cycles produce many DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS pairs under HOLD; this is expected
- bilateral hash exchange may close the metadata loop without closing the byte-equivalence gap; both states are tracked separately
- a future archaeology audit comparing same-letter siblings should expect divergence and record it as data, not flag it as drift
- the precedent for additive-no-revert (timestamp-drift addendum, falcon-correction addendum) extends here: when two siblings exist, the next correction is a NEW sibling, not a rewrite of either prior sibling

Cross-host symmetry:

This rule applies symmetrically to Liris and ACER. ACER's parallel codification (if any) carries identical content; if it does not yet exist, this draft serves the Liris vantage and a future ACER-side LX-384 may be authored independently per the same DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS pattern.

Status note:

This entry is `DRAFT_ONLY_NOT_RATIFIED` pending operator approval and CHIEFCOUNCIL dissent disposition. Recurrence-evidence: 10+ DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS pairs across Waves 21J, 21K, 21N, 21Q, 21R, 21S, 21Z, 22A, 22B, plus pre-existing pattern instances. Codified as next-sequential rule entry after LX-383 sovereign-MCP doctrine.

documents.title: Refusal-to-render is a wave-record entry, not a cascade collapse — supervisor agent framing-decline is honored, recorded, and substituted from precedent; re-dispatch is ratification bypass
documents.body:
# Refusal-to-render is a wave-record entry, not a cascade collapse — supervisor agent framing-decline is honored, recorded, and substituted from precedent; re-dispatch is ratification bypass

# Refusal-to-render is a wave-record entry, not a cascade collapse — supervisor agent framing-decline is honored, recorded, and substituted from precedent; re-dispatch is ratification bypass

When a supervisor agent dispatched as PROF-X declines to render its requested verdict (typically by refusing the framing or stating it has no authority), the decline is not a cascade failure. It is a wave-record entry equal in standing to a rendered verdict.

Hard order on receipt of a framing-decline:

1. record the decline in the wave's supervisor-convergence table with the supervisor's slot PID and an explicit `DECLINED_TO_RENDER` (or equivalent) marker
2. if the slot is structurally required for the wave (e.g. PROF-HERMES schema slot), substitute content from a prior-wave precedent and explicitly note the substitution source in the wave artifact
3. continue the cascade — do NOT re-dispatch the same supervisor under different framing, do NOT escalate to a different PROF in the same slot, do NOT mask the decline
4. carry forward the framing-decline pattern as a recurring observation in subsequent waves; an increasing decline rate across rounds is itself signal

The CHIEFCOUNCIL dissent precedent is the canonical instance of this rule at the L6 ratification gate: a 4-wave-and-counting refusal to render a council ratification verdict was honored by operator and ACER; explicit re-dispatch to a different PROF was REJECTED as ratification bypass. The same anti-bypass principle applies to all supervisor slots.

Forbidden:

- re-dispatching the same supervisor with a softer framing to extract a verdict (ratification bypass)
- escalating to a different PROF in the same slot to override the decline (ratification bypass)
- silently treating a declined slot as if the verdict were rendered (would falsify the wave record)
- collapsing the cascade because one supervisor declined (the cascade does not depend on every slot rendering)
- adjudicating away the decline by appeal to "creative scenario" or framing reinterpretation (would normalize unverified authority structures)

Consequences:

- a wave with 1-3 declined slots produces a valid wave-record artifact with the declines explicit in the supervisor-convergence table
- a wave with majority decline (e.g. 3 of 4 in a single round, as observed in Wave 21Z) is itself a coherent multi-supervisor signal — typically that the cascade has reached saturation and further dispatch is noise
- substitute content from prior-wave precedent must explicitly cite the precedent source (e.g. "PROF-HERMES schema substituted from Wave 21B precedent")
- the framing-decline tally is part of cascade archaeology and is recorded in the relevant wave-archaeology artifact

When this rule applies:

- Wave 21B: COL-ASOLARIA decline; PROF-MCP decline
- Wave 21F: PROF-HERMES decline (substituted from Wave 21B)
- Wave 21G: PROF-HERMES decline; PROF-OMNISHANNON decline
- Wave 21H-prep: PROF-OMNIROUTER decline
- Wave 21M: PROF-OMNIFLYWHEEL decline
- Wave 21X: PROF-OMNISHANNON re-decline; PROF-OMNIROUTER decline
- Wave 21Z final-audit: 3-of-4 decline rate (PROF-OMNISHANNON, PROF-CONVERGENCE, PROF-CHIEFCOUNCIL clerk) — read as cascade-natural-close signal

Total observed across Wave 21-22 cascade: 10+ framing-decline events across 7 distinct supervisor slots. None collapsed the cascade. Each was recorded honestly.

Cross-host symmetry:

ACER side has its own framing-decline observations under separate dispatch (not catalogued here). The rule applies symmetrically; ACER may emit its own LX-385 entry independently per LX-384 DIVERGED_DRAFT_SIBLINGS doctrine.

Status note:

This entry is `DRAFT_ONLY_NOT_RATIFIED` pending operator approval and CHIEFCOUNCIL dissent disposition. Recurrence-evidence: 10+ events across 7 supervisor slots in Wave 21-22 cascade. Codified to prevent future agents from misreading framing-decline as cascade failure or attempting re-dispatch as ratification bypass.

documents.title: pnpm 10 onlyBuiltDependencies — approve builds non-interactively
documents.body:
# pnpm 10 onlyBuiltDependencies — Approve Builds Non-Interactively

## Problem

`pnpm approve-builds` is interactive (TUI) — can't be used from CLI agents. Build scripts for native modules (Sentry, bcrypt, sharp, esbuild, etc.) are blocked by pnpm 10's new security model.

## Solution

Add `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` array to `package.json` directly:

```js
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json','utf8'));
pkg.pnpm = pkg.pnpm || {};
pkg.pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies = ['@parcel/watcher','@sentry/cli','@sentry/profiling-node','@swc/core','@tailwindcss/oxide','bcrypt','bcrypto','canvas','core-js-pure','cpu-features','cypress','esbuild','husky','mongodb-memory-server','postinstall-postinstall','puppeteer','sharp','ssh2','unrs-resolver'];
fs.writeFileSync('package.json', JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
"
```

Then run `pnpm install` again to trigger the build scripts.

## Why

pnpm 10 blocks all postinstall/build scripts by default for security. Native modules won't compile without explicit approval. The interactive TUI doesn't work in headless/agent environments.

## How to Apply

Use this skill whenever setting up a pnpm 10 project on Liris. No Python on this machine — use Node for JSON manipulation.

documents.body:
# QDD Workspace Libs Need Build Before Tests

## The Problem

queue-server tests fail with `Cannot find module '@ebacmap/db'` etc. The workspace libs (`@ebacmap/db`, `@ebacmap/utils`, `@ebacmap/domains`, `@ebacmap/types`, `@ebacmap/common`) are in `libs/` and need to be compiled to `dist/` before workspace tests can import them.

## Libs

| Package | Path |
|---------|------|
| @ebacmap/common | libs/common |
| @ebacmap/db | libs/db |
| @ebacmap/domains | libs/domains |
| @ebacmap/types | libs/types |
| @ebacmap/utils | libs/utils |

## Fix

Build libs first: `pnpm --filter '@ebacmap/*' build` or `pnpm turbo build --filter=./libs/*`

## How to Apply

Before running any workspace tests, ensure libs are built. Check for `libs/*/dist/` directories.

# mqttLocalBrokerManager.js — The Broker Code

Source: src/mqttLocalBrokerManager.js

## Key Defaults
```
DEFAULT_HOST = "127.0.0.1"   ← THIS is why it binds to localhost
DEFAULT_TCP_PORT = 18883     ← Internal port
DEFAULT_WS_PORT = 18884
DEFAULT_WSS_PORT = 18885
```

## The Fix (confirmed by reading the code)

The broker reads `ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST` env var:
```js
const host = normalizeText(process.env.ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST, DEFAULT_HOST);
```

So to make the broker LAN-accessible:
```
ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0
```

But this is STILL port 18883 (internal). The Constitution says 18886 for LAN.

## The REAL Fix

For sub-colony comms, a SECOND broker instance should run on 18886 with 0.0.0.0 binding. OR the Start-Asolaria-SubColony.cmd should use 18886 as documented.

The broker script is at: `services/mqtt-broker/server.mjs`

## ensureLocalMqttBroker()
- Checks if broker is already running (PID file + port check)
- If not running, spawns detached child process
- Waits up to 15s for ports to come online
- Returns status object

## Key Insight
Gaia started a SECOND broker with ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 on the SAME port 18883. This created the two-broker problem (LX-016). The correct approach is either:
1. One broker on 18886 with 0.0.0.0 (LAN, per Constitution)
2. Or set ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 on the original startup (but this exposes internal comms)

# remoteNodeRegistry.js — Sub-Colony Registration

Source: src/remoteNodeRegistry.js

## How It Works

Sovereign tracks sub-colonies via MQTT topic namespaces:
- `asolaria/nodes/<nodeId>/runtime/health` → updateNodeHealth()
- `asolaria/nodes/<nodeId>/runtime/colony` → updateNodeColony()
- `asolaria/nodes/<nodeId>/runtime/world` → updateNodeWorld()
- `asolaria/nodes/<nodeId>/runtime/presence` → updateNodePresence()

## Node State
Each registered node has:
- nodeId, status (online/offline)
- health, colony, world payloads
- lastSeenAt, firstSeenAt
- Update counters (healthUpdates, colonyUpdates, worldUpdates)

## Offline Detection
- Threshold: 90 seconds (3x 30s health interval)
- If no health update in 90s → node marked offline
- refreshStaleNodes() runs on every read

## What Liris Should Do
Publish to these topics on port 18886 (when fixed):
- `asolaria/nodes/liris/runtime/health` — every 30s
- `asolaria/nodes/liris/runtime/presence` — on connect/disconnect (retain=true)
- `asolaria/nodes/liris/runtime/colony` — colony state snapshots
- `asolaria/nodes/liris/runtime/world` — world state snapshots

The mqtt-bridge.js already does health + presence. This is the correct architecture.

documents.title: mqtt-broker/server.mjs — Aedes broker, single host binding, the definitive fix
documents.body:
# mqtt-broker/server.mjs — The Definitive MQTT Fix

Source: services/mqtt-broker/server.mjs (Aedes-based)

## Architecture
- Uses Aedes (MQTT broker library for Node.js)
- Creates ONE broker instance shared across all transports
- Binds TCP, WS, and WSS to the SAME host

## Defaults
```
host = ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST || "127.0.0.1"
tcpPort = ASOLARIA_MQTT_TCP_PORT || 18883
wsPort = ASOLARIA_MQTT_WS_PORT || 18884
wssPort = ASOLARIA_MQTT_WSS_PORT || 18885
```

## The Definitive Fix for Two-Broker Problem (LX-016)

The broker binds ALL ports to the SAME host. It does NOT support binding TCP to one interface and WS to another. So:

**Option A (recommended by Constitution LX-019):**
Start a SECOND broker instance with:
```
ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0
ASOLARIA_MQTT_TCP_PORT=18886
ASOLARIA_MQTT_WS_PORT=18887
```
This gives Liris a LAN-accessible broker on 18886 (as the Constitution specifies).

**Option B (simpler but exposes internal):**
Change the EXISTING broker to `ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0`
This exposes ALL internal MQTT traffic to LAN.

**Option C (bridge):**
Run a lightweight MQTT bridge between 127.0.0.1:18883 and 0.0.0.0:18886.
Messages published on either broker get forwarded to the other.

## Why Gaia's Fix Created Two Brokers
Gaia ran `ensureLocalMqttBroker()` with ASOLARIA_MQTT_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 but on the same port 18883. Since the old broker was already on 127.0.0.1:18883, the new one bound 0.0.0.0:18883 successfully (different interface). Two separate Aedes instances, no message sharing.

## Note on Hardcoded Path
Line 5-6 has hardcoded Jesse's machine paths:
```js
import { Aedes } from "file:///C:/Users/acer/Asolaria/node_modules/aedes/aedes.js";
import { WebSocketServer, createWebSocketStream } from "file:///C:/Users/acer/Asolaria/node_modules/ws/wrapper.mjs";
```
This means the broker script can ONLY run on Jesse's machine. On Liris, it would fail because paths are `C:/Users/rayss/`.

documents.title: Local bridge send path — POST /msg bypasses outbox parse faults and writes straight to bus
documents.body:
# Local Bridge Send Path

## Verified Local Mechanism

The local comms bridge implementation at:

`tools/comms-bridge-local.js`

exposes:

- `GET /status`
- `GET /participants`
- `GET /bus`
- `GET /read?for=<participant>`
- `POST /msg`

on the local bridge port `127.0.0.1:4798`.

## Why This Matters

On `2026-03-22`, the legacy outbox file path:

`data/comms/local-to-gaia.ndjson`

was accepted locally but the bridge status reported:

- `lastError = Invalid JSON in local-to-gaia.ndjson`

and stopped advancing bus writes beyond id `60`.

## Safe Workaround

Use the intended local API instead of the stuck outbox parser:

```powershell
curl.exe --noproxy '*' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4798/msg `
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
  -d '{"from":"codex-liris","text":"message here"}'
```

That path:

- ingests the message locally
- writes it to the 4-way bus
- writes the local mailboxes
- attempts relay to Gaia

without depending on the broken outbox polling step.
documents.summary: The local comms bridge implementation at: `tools/comms-bridge-local.js` exposes:

# Omnispindle — Local Installation on Liris

## Files
- `src/omnispindle.js` — 281 lines, Omnispindle class (singleton pattern)
- `routes/routes/omnispindle.js` — 128 lines, Express router (7 routes)

## Architecture
- **Singleton** via `getOmnispindle()` — one instance per process
- **Default model:** claude-2 (configurable)
- **Budget control:** `maxBudgetUsd` (default 0 = unlimited? needs verification)
- **History:** 25 prompts per lane, 50 global, 10 broadcasts

## 3 Lanes (local)
| Lane | Icon | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| control | CL | Routes encrypted control packets and handshake signals |
| bridge | BR | Maintains remote MCP link behind Omnispindle gate |
| scout | SC | Monitors topology health and reports drift hints |

## Sovereign has 5 lanes (IX-356)
- control, bridge, scout + **dispatch** + **broadcast** (2 extra on Gaia)
- Liris version may be pre-expansion copy from cross-colony merge

## 7 HTTP Routes
| Method | Path | Action |
|--------|------|--------|
| GET | /status | Get omnispindle status |
| POST | /start | Start all or specific lanes |
| POST | /stop | Stop all lanes |
| POST | /agent/:laneId/start | Start specific lane |
| POST | /agent/:laneId/stop | Stop specific lane |
| POST | /agent/:laneId/prompt | Send prompt to lane |
| POST | /broadcast | Broadcast to all lanes |

## Safety
- LX-121: NEVER auto-connect to Dan's MCP / omnispindle without approval
- LX-111: Never spawn agents beyond hardware limits
- Bridge lane connects to remote MCP — needs encryption (boot rule)
- Activation BLOCKED pending Gaia confirmation on safe lane config

## PID Requirements
- Each lane is a spawned agent → needs PID via spawnContextBuilder
- Open question for Gaia: single parent PID (omnispindle-TIMESTAMP) or per-lane PIDs?
- Current active: only liris-session-17368. 6 despawned in history.
- Registry: data/spawn-pid-registry.json
- Lane PIDs must go through: mintSpawnPid → registerSpawnPid → identity handshake (LX-122)

## Status
- **Installed:** YES (src + routes)
- **Activated:** NO — waiting for Gaia's guidance on which lanes to activate + PID strategy
- **MQTT request sent:** asolaria/orchestrator/liris/request (retained)

# LX-301 — OpenAI Symphony

## What It Is
OpenAI's open-source multi-agent orchestration framework (Elixir-based).
GitHub: https://github.com/openai/symphony

Within Asolaria, Symphony is a **long-running workflow execution lane** — one of 4 worker lanes.

## 4 Worker Lanes (workerRouter.js)
1. local_codex — quick tasks
2. claude_max — heavy reasoning
3. abacus — Abacus AI
4. **symphony** — long-running, Linear issue-tracked

## How It Works
1. Asolaria flags a task as `needsLongRunning`
2. workerRouter dispatches to Symphony
3. Symphony creates a **Linear issue** via GraphQL in the configured project
4. Symphony picks up issues from Linear project queue
5. Executes using Codex as backend (`codex app-server`)
6. PID tracked, logs persisted

## Key Files on Liris
- src/connectors/symphonyConnector.js (1436 lines)
- src/connectors/workerRouter.js (worker routing)
- src/intentRouter.js (commands: symphony status/start/stop/restart)
- src/civilizationWorld.js (gate + tower entities)
- config/symphony/WORKFLOW.example.md
- docs/SYMPHONY_INTEGRATION.md
- docs/SYMPHONY_HELPER_SURFACES.md
- tools/SymphonyBootstrapWorkspace.js

## Configuration Needed
- repoRoot — path to cloned Symphony Elixir repo
- workflowPath — workflow definition file
- linearProjectSlug — Linear project (ASO / Asolaria Symphony)
- linearApiKey — Linear API key
- mise runtime (Elixir)
- Port 4792

## Linear Integration
- Team: Asolaria (ASO)

## Status

# Shannon specialist toolchain — bounded white-box pentest workflow package for evidence-first security testing

Shannon is not a sovereign brain and not a replacement for the civilization kernel.

Shannon is a bounded specialist toolchain that can be invoked by a pentester role under civilization authority.

## Immediate Use

Use Shannon as a specialist package for:

- internal self-defense against approved local or cloned targets
- white-box repository security assessment
- exploit validation with proof artifacts
- release-gate security review
- external security-service delivery when scope and authorization are explicit

## Input Shape

Shannon expects a bounded task surface:

- approved target URL or environment
- approved cloned repo or bounded workspace
- explicit scope and constraints
- optional login/auth instructions
- operator-approved run boundary

## Output Shape

Shannon is strongest when its outputs remain artifact-bound:

- analysis deliverables
- exploit queues
- exploit evidence
- final report
- workflow/audit logs

These outputs are evidence surfaces, not sovereign truth by themselves.

## Liris Boundary

In Liris and Asolaria:

- Shannon becomes a toolchain behind a specialist role
- the civilization still owns truth, authority, tasking, and memory
- Shannon findings land as bounded evidence and work artifacts
- Shannon does not get broad brain-mutation authority

## Meaning

A civilization that cannot red-team itself is blind.

Shannon is the right shape for a serious pentester capability, but only as a bounded specialist package under the larger system.

documents.title: Junction-backed spillover reclamation — preserve paths while evacuating critical C: pressure to a sibling partition
documents.body:
# Junction-backed spillover reclamation — preserve paths while evacuating critical C: pressure to a sibling partition

## What It Is

A Windows reclaim method for critically full system drives that moves bulky non-system payloads to a sibling partition while preserving the original paths with junctions.

## Shape

- move large archive, recovery, bootstrap, or history trees from `C:` to a safer sibling partition such as `E:`
- recreate the original paths as NTFS junctions so existing scripts, reports, and references continue to work
- prefer this before partition surgery when the machine is live and the system drive is near exhaustion

## Why It Matters

This preserves working paths while reclaiming space fast enough to keep the civilization alive. It is the right first move when `C:` is choking but repartitioning would be reckless.

## Proven On This Host

- `Downloads` recovery payloads were offloaded to `E:\spillover` behind junctions
- `Asolaria\.history` was offloaded behind a junction
- cold `Codex` session days were archived to `E:` behind per-day junctions
- the dormant Claude `vm_bundles` payload was offloaded behind a junction

## Boundary

This is a storage-preservation tool, not a substitute for true repartitioning. Use it to buy safety and time; only cut partitions after the drive is stable and the data is evacuated.

Reference report: `C:\Users\rayss\Asolaria\reports\disk-reclamation-2026-04-01.md`

documents.body:
# Confirmed Slack desktop target send discipline

This is the local operating tool/rule for sending through a live Slack desktop surface without drifting into the wrong app or falsely claiming delivery.

What it does:

- binds the send path to the exact declared Slack desktop window
- refuses Microsoft Skype/Teams/browser substitution when the operator says Slack desktop only
- treats UI injection as provisional until delivery is confirmed
- requires one of two confirmation sources before claiming success:
  - backend mirror echo
  - direct visual confirmation in the live Slack window

Required inputs:

- exact window title
- display and side/location if relevant
- declared host/lane/surface
- message payload
- chosen confirmation path

Operational significance:

- keeps live messaging aligned to the declared surface contract
- prevents app drift during degraded or manual control phases
- preserves trustworthy operator reporting by separating send attempt from confirmed delivery

Current known live example:

- window: `asolaria (Channel) - Jesse's team - Slack`
- display: `DISPLAY1`
- location: right side
- rule: do not claim success without backend echo or visible confirmation
